review_notes: I read the whole file. It is a generated numeric-certificate file. It has a list of log-entropy certificates, an index lookup, 36 `decide +kernel` coverage lemmas, and `Ball.Encloses` soundness lemmas. It has no `@[simp]` declarations, no simp sets, and no rewrite rules that could loop or compete. The only simp call is the local `simp only [checkLog, Bool.and_eq_true]` in `CA4_6_6I1PairMassTermLog_sound`. That call is explicit and does not depend on a global simp set. The `_sound` lemmas are stated for specific constants, with the `Encloses` predicate applied to a named ball. They are used by direct term application, so adding simp attributes would add no canonical form and could cause unwanted unfolding of the huge rational literals. I found no justified simp-interface problem. I did not inspect the imported files, and I did not check how downstream files use these declarations.
